title: Where Romans wrote
excerpt: I mapped 203,466 Latin inscriptions through time. Under the Severans the empire carved 2.2 times as many a year as in AD 250 to 300; ages on tombstones were rounded to fives; and soldiers' stated homes were a median 674 km from their stones.
seo_description: 203,466 Latin inscriptions mapped through time: the rise and fall of Roman writing, rounded ages on tombstones and soldiers far from home.
header_alt: Title card on pale paper reading 'Where Romans wrote' beside a map of the Roman Empire covered in orange hexagons, darkest in central Italy and along the Rhine.
